cues.en: This program is presented by University of California Television. Like what you learn? Visit our website or follow us on Facebook and Twitter to keep up with the latest UCTV programs. Good evening everyone. Welcome again to our penultimate class in this semester's course on nutrition. A reminder that next week we'll be talking about vitamins and minerals and vitamin and mineral supplements so please join us for that last class.
cues.zh: 本节目由加州大学电视呈现。喜欢所学内容吗？访问我们的网站，或在Facebook和Twitter上关注我们，以获取UCTV最新节目。大家晚上好。欢迎再次来到本学期营养学课程的倒数第二堂课。提醒一下，下周我们将讨论维生素和矿物质以及维生素和矿物质补充剂，请参加最后一堂课。

cues.en: Dr. Jeffrey Tice will be the professor joining us that evening. Tonight we have what I guess for some of you has been the lecture you've been waiting for since the beginning. Dr. Lustig.
cues.zh: 杰弗里·泰斯博士将作为教授加入我们那天晚上。今晚我们有我想对你们一些人来说从一开始就在等待的讲座。勒斯蒂格博士。

cues.en: gave a similar lecture in 2009. Little did we know at the time that it would have 3.5 million downloads since then, but it was in this room at a course very similar to this that I also chaired. And it's really, I think, changed his life more than anything else. But I think the hope is that it's also changed the field and the topic and the policies and the politics of what we're going to talk about tonight.
cues.zh: 在2009年做过类似的讲座。当时我们不知道它从那以后会有350万次下载，但就是在那个房间，在一个与这个非常相似的课程中，我也是主持人。我认为这真的比其他任何事都更改变了他的生活。但我认为希望是它也改变了领域和主题以及我们今晚要谈论的政策和政治。

cues.en: Many of you know Dr. Lustig is an internationally known neuroendocrinologist in pediatrics.
cues.zh: 你们很多人知道勒斯蒂格博士是国际知名的儿科神经内分泌学家。

cues.en: He trained for part of his time at UCSF, then went back east to do clinical neuroendocrinology and came back to UCSF in 2001, where he's continued to do his clinical science on factors that control appetite, particularly the interaction between the hormones of insulin, leptin, ghrelin, and appetite control and the metabolic syndrome and obesity.
cues.zh: 他在UCSF部分时间接受培训，然后去东海岸做临床神经内分泌学，并于2001年回到UCSF，在那里他继续做关于控制食欲因素的临床科学，特别是胰岛素、瘦素、胃饥饿素激素与食欲控制和代谢综合征及肥胖之间的相互作用。

cues.en: More recently, in part around the time of the video, and certainly in the four years since, Rob has become an international leader in the efforts to improve our nutrition, not only in the United States, but around the world. He's focused
cues.zh: 最近，部分是在那段视频前后，当然也是在那之后的四年里，Rob 已成为改善我们营养状况的努力中的国际领军人物，不仅在美国，也在全世界。他一直专注于

cues.en: a larger part by putting a real microscope on the issues of fructose and sugar in general and refined foods in general, the relationship to dietary fiber and many of the other topics that we've been talking about over the course of the course. Rob just returned from Europe.
cues.zh: 其中很大一部分，是通过真正深入审视果糖以及一般意义上的糖和精制食品的问题、它们与膳食纤维的关系，以及我们在课程中一直在讨论的许多其他话题。Rob 刚从欧洲回来。

cues.en: In fact, arrived here at five o'clock this evening. We think he had dinner. We know he hasn't had sleep. It's four o'clock Europe time for him, so this was really a heroic effort. Our fingers were crossed that all the flights would be on time, and I'm very pleased, more than you can imagine, that he's here tonight, because I didn't want to give this lecture as well.
cues.zh: 事实上，他今晚五点到这儿。我们觉得他吃过晚饭了。我们知道他还没睡觉。对他来说是欧洲时间四点，所以这真是英雄般的努力。我们一直祈愿所有航班准点，我今晚他能来，我高兴得超出你们想象，因为我也不想再来讲这一场。

cues.en: But in addition to his work, Rob recently took a sabbatical in order to further this work and spend a large part of that time at Hastings School of Law, getting a Master of Studies in Law. And part of his aspiration, I think, is really to add his legal training now to his science and medical training to continue to advocate for good nutrition around the world.
cues.zh: 但除了他的工作，Rob 最近还休了学术假，以推进这项工作，并把其中很大一部分时间花在 Hastings 法学院，攻读法律研究硕士。我认为，他的部分抱负确实是把现在的法律训练与他的科学和医学训练结合起来，继续在全世界倡导良好营养。

cues.en: We're very anxious to hear about his newest thoughts on this topic. We've entitled the talk the same title as his best-selling book, Fat Chance, and added the subtitle, Fructose 2.0. Rob? Thank you, Bobby, and thank all of you for coming. To some extent, this is sort of like deja vu all over again.
cues.zh: 我们非常渴望听到他关于这个话题的最新想法。我们把演讲题目定得与他畅销书《Fat Chance》同名，并加了副标题“Fructose 2.0”。Rob？谢谢，Bobby，也谢谢大家前来。某种程度上，这有点像又一次似曾相识。

cues.en: having done this four years ago and it really did change my life and hopefully it changed a few people's lives in the audience and certainly around the world. I still get emails from that video today, people who have seen it for the first time. That video, we're going to refer back to it to some extent tonight because I am not going to redo the biochemistry. There's no point in doing it twice.
cues.zh: 四年前我做过这件事，它确实改变了我的人生。希望它也改变了在场观众中一些人的人生，当然也改变了世界各地一些人的人生。直到今天，我仍然会收到关于那段视频的邮件，有些人刚刚第一次看到了它。今晚我们还会在一定程度上回顾那段视频，因为我不会重新讲一遍生物化学，毕竟同样的内容没必要讲两次。

cues.en: What we're going to talk tonight about is primarily the physiology. So in a sense, the two videos will end up being complementary on YouTube, and hopefully people who watch it will end up watching both. So keep that in mind.
cues.zh: 今晚我们主要要讲的是生理学。所以从某种意义上说，这两段视频在 YouTube 上会形成互补，希望看过其中一段的人最终也会把另一段看完。请记住这一点。

cues.en: All right. Well, a lot's happened in four years and the data just keeps rolling in and unfortunately for us, all the data is pretty awful. So you'll see why as we go and I will try to delineate that as we go. So first of all, I have no disclosures. No food industry is putting me up to this. I'm going to be sure of that. All right. So here's the past. This is 2001. Six million kids are seriously overweight. Well,
cues.zh: 好，四年里发生了很多事，数据也在不断涌入。但遗憾的是，对我们来说，所有数据都相当糟糕。接下来你们就会明白原因，我也会边讲边把这些情况解释清楚。首先，我没有任何利益披露。没有任何食品行业的企业资助或指使我来讲这些。对此我很确定。好，这是过去的情况。这是 2001 年，当时有 600 万儿童严重超重。嗯，

cues.en: With all of the media attention, with all of the NIH money, with all of the clinical programs, and with Michelle Obama's vegetable gardens, we are now up to 20 million. Here's the present. Currently, there are 30% more obese people on the planet than undernourished people. And this has happened only within 15 years, because 15 years ago it was exactly the opposite. And it's occurring in countries that still have undernutrition. So how do you explain that?
cues.zh: 媒体的广泛关注、NIH 的资金投入、各种临床项目，再加上 Michelle Obama 的蔬菜园，如今这个数字已经上升到 2000 万。这是现在的情况。目前，全球肥胖人口比营养不良人口多 30%。而这一切只发生在 15 年之内，因为 15 年前，情况恰恰相反。而且，这种现象还发生在那些仍然存在营养不良的国家。那该如何解释呢？

cues.en: other than to say, that can't be behavior, that's got to be an exposure. This looks like any standard pandemic, influenza, typhoid, etc. This looks like a microbial phenomenon rather than a behavior phenomenon. We're going to go there. 366 million diabetics walking the Earth, that's 5 percent of the world's population, and they are chewing through all the healthcare resources.
cues.zh: 只能说，这不可能是行为，肯定是暴露。这看起来像任何标准流行病——流感、伤寒等等。这看起来是微生物现象，而不是行为现象。我们接下来就讲这个。全球有3.66亿糖尿病患者，占世界人口5%，他们正在消耗所有医疗资源。

cues.en: This was just three months ago. Diabetes cost the US $245 billion. Now, if we could recoup even a fraction of that, we wouldn't even need health care reform. In fact, it's been suggested that we wouldn't even need financial reform. 41 percent rise in five years. This is going up so fast it makes your head spin. Here's the future if we do nothing.
cues.zh: 这只是三个月前的事。糖尿病让美国付出了2450亿美元。现在，哪怕能收回其中一小部分，我们甚至都不需要医疗改革。事实上，有人提出，我们甚至不需要金融改革。五年内上升41%。涨得太快，让人头晕目眩。如果我们什么都不做，未来就是这样。

cues.en: Experts predict 165 million Americans, 42% will be obese by the year 2030. 100 million Americans, that'll be 33% will have diabetes by 2050, but fear not because it won't really matter because Medicare will be broke by 2026. So as the soup Nazi one said, no health care for you. Well, the fact of the matter is I'm going to be 69 in 2026 and I want my freaking Medicare.
cues.zh: 专家预测，到2030年，1.65亿美国人、也就是42%，将患上肥胖症。到2050年，1亿美国人、也就是33%，将患上糖尿病；但别担心，因为那其实不重要，因为Medicare到2026年就会破产。所以，正如Soup Nazi所说：不给你医保。可事实是，到2026年我就69岁了，我要我该死的Medicare。

cues.en: So should you all, the point is we have to do something different. You know the old adage, right? The definition of insanity is doing the same thing over and over again and expecting a different result. Well, I am here to tell you for the last 30 years we have done the same thing over and over and over again and there has been no change in the result. So we have to rethink this. We have to reframe the argument and that's what we're going to try to do tonight. I'm going to do it right now. So here's.
cues.zh: 你们所有人也都该要，重点是，我们必须做出不同的改变。你知道那句老话吧？精神错乱的定义，就是一遍又一遍做同样的事，却期待不同结果。我来告诉你们：过去30年，我们一遍又一遍、一遍又一遍地做同样的事，结果没有任何变化。所以我们必须重新思考。我们必须重新构建这个论点，这就是今晚我们要尝试做的事。我现在就开始。那么，开始吧。

cues.en: the way people view this issue. This is a Venn diagram of all the adults in America. 30 percent obese over here and 70 percent normal weight over here. Everybody assumes that the problem is this group over here because 80 percent of the obese population is sick in some fashion.
cues.zh: 人们对这个问题的看法是这样的。这是美国所有成年人的维恩图。这边30%是肥胖人群，那边70%是正常体重人群。大家都以为问题出在这边这群人身上，因为80%的肥胖人群在某种程度上是不健康的。

cues.en: with type 2 diabetes, lipid problems, hypertension, cardiovascular disease, cancer, dementia, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease, polycystic ovarian disease, etc., etc. If you do the math on this, that's 80 percent of 30 percent of 240 million, that's 57 million sick, and it's those 57 million that are bankrupting the country. It's the obese person's fault only. That's the way everyone views this. This is wrong.
cues.zh: 2型糖尿病、血脂问题、高血压、心血管疾病、癌症、痴呆、非酒精性脂肪肝病、多囊卵巢疾病等等。如果你算一下，那是2.4亿人中30%的80%，也就是5700万病人，正是这5700万人让这个国家破产。大家认为这全是肥胖者的错。所有人都是这么看的。这是错的。

cues.en: This is a mistake. This is a disaster, actually, because it's not correct. Here's the real story. In fact, 20% of the obese population is completely metabolically normal. They have normal insulin dynamics. They don't get sick. They will live a completely normal life, die at a completely normal age, cost the taxpayer nothing. They're just fat. Conversely...
cues.zh: 这是个错误。实际上这是个灾难，因为这不正确。真实情况是这样的。事实上，20%的肥胖人群代谢完全正常。他们的胰岛素动态正常。他们不会生病。他们会过着完全正常的生活，在完全正常的年龄去世，不给纳税人增加任何负担。他们只是胖而已。反过来说……

cues.en: up to 40 percent of the normal weight population have the exact same metabolic dysfunction that the obese do, they're just normal weight. So they don't even know they're sick until it's too late. Because normal weight people get type 2 diabetes, they get hypertension, they get dyslipidemia, they get cardiovascular disease, they get cancer, they get dementia, etc. So when you do the math on that, that's another 67 million. So that's actually outclassing the obese. So the total is 124 million, that's more than half.
cues.zh: 高达40%的正常体重人群有着和肥胖者完全相同的代谢功能障碍，他们只是体重正常。所以他们甚至不知道自己生病了，直到为时已晚。因为正常体重的人也会得2型糖尿病、高血压、血脂异常、心血管疾病、癌症、痴呆等等。所以算下来，那又是6700万人。实际上这超过了肥胖人群。总数是1.24亿，超过了一半。

cues.en: of all of America. Now, you may remember HIV. Remember HIV? When did HIV become a public health crisis? In the 80s? No, not in the 80s. In 1991. 1979, patient zero, so we first learned about the diagnosis. Throughout the entire 80s, it was all about the gays and the addicts.
cues.zh: 在美国全国范围内。现在，你们可能还记得HIV。记得HIV吗？HIV什么时候成为公共卫生危机的？80年代？不，不是80年代。是1991年。1979年，零号病人，所以我们首次得知了这个诊断。整个80年代，这事都只关乎同性恋和吸毒者。

cues.en: And it was always, well, it's their problem, their personal responsibility, their behavior, their fault. And then something happened in 1991. Anybody know what it was? Magic Johnson. Magic Johnson got HIV. And all of a sudden, everybody went, holy mother, you know what?
cues.zh: 一直都是，嗯，那是他们的问题，他们的个人责任，他们的行为，他们的错。然后1991年发生了一件事。有人知道是什么吗？魔术师约翰逊。魔术师约翰逊感染了HIV。突然间，所有人都惊呼，我的天哪，你知道吗？

cues.en: And everybody realized, you know what? Everyone's at risk. And all of a sudden, it became a public health crisis. So when does a personal responsibility issue become a public health crisis? And that's what we're going to talk about tonight, because this is a public health crisis. Here's the slide that demonstrates the phenomenon. So here are two equally weighted adult men. Which one's healthy and which one's sick? Anybody? No? The one on the...
cues.zh: 所有人都意识到，你知道吗？每个人都有风险。突然间，这就成了公共卫生危机。那么，个人责任问题何时变成公共卫生危机？这就是我们今晚要讨论的，因为这就是一场公共卫生危机。这张幻灯片展示了这个现象。这里有两个体重相当的成年男性。哪个健康，哪个生病？有人知道吗？不知道？下面那个……

cues.en: Bottom is sick, right? He's sick. Why? All that visceral fat, all that fat surrounding the organs. See, this guy over here, he's got big love handles, but, you know, so what? In fact, this is perfectly healthy. It's no problem, because subcutaneous fat is actually kind of good for you. There are actually studies that show more subcutaneous fat, more longevity. Whereas this stuff, this is the bad stuff, this is the poison stuff over here. So the fact is, standing on a scale doesn't tell you where your fat is.
cues.zh: 下面那个生病了，对吧？他病了。为什么？那么多内脏脂肪，那么多环绕器官的脂肪。看，这边这位，他有大大的腰间赘肉，但是，那又怎样？事实上，这完全健康。没问题，因为皮下脂肪其实对你有点好处。实际上有研究表明，皮下脂肪越多，越长寿。而这些东西，这是坏东西，这是有毒的东西。所以事实是，站在秤上并不能告诉你脂肪在哪里。

cues.en: What does? Well, your waist circumference is a good start, and then there are some lab tests you can do as well. The bottom line is, there are a lot of normal way people who have this phenomenon called toffee. Thin on the outside, fat on the inside. Probably some right here in the audience. They get type 2 diabetes, they get dyslipidemia, they get hypertension, etc. You get the picture? Everyone's at risk because everyone's exposed. The question is, what is it you're exposed to?
cues.zh: 那怎么判断呢？腰围是个不错的起点，然后还有一些实验室检查可以做。关键是，很多外表正常的人都有这种现象，叫做TOFI。外表瘦，内里胖。可能在座的观众里就有。他们会得2型糖尿病、血脂异常、高血压等等。明白了吗？每个人都有风险，因为每个人都暴露在风险中。问题是，你暴露在什么之中？

cues.en: because obesity is not the problem. It never was. They want you to think it's the problem, but it ain't the problem. What is the problem? Metabolic syndrome is the problem. The cluster of diseases that I've just described to you because that's where all the money goes. Obesity costs almost nothing. Metabolic syndrome is 75 percent of all healthcare costs today. There's the list right there. Everybody with me now? Do I have your attention?
cues.zh: 因为肥胖不是问题。从来都不是。他们想让你以为这是问题，但它不是。问题是什么？代谢综合征才是问题。就是我刚才描述的那一组疾病，因为钱都花在那里了。肥胖几乎不花什么钱。代谢综合征占了当今所有医疗费用的75%。清单就在那里。大家都跟上了吗？我引起你们的注意了吗？

cues.en: How does this work? This actually is a redundancy from the previous YouTube video, so I apologize for that. It has to do with how you view the question of obesity and what does it mean. Of course, obesity obeys the first law of thermodynamics and I don't argue that. The total energy inside a closed system remains constant. It's a law.
cues.zh: 这是怎么回事？这部分其实和之前的YouTube视频有重复，所以我道个歉。这关乎你如何看待肥胖这个问题以及它意味着什么。当然，肥胖遵守热力学第一定律，我不否认这一点。封闭系统内的总能量保持不变。这是一条定律。

cues.en: If I didn't believe in the first law of thermodynamics, you'd have me ridden out on a rail. I would be the ultimate heretic and zealot, and I would be discredited. Of course, I believe in the first law of thermodynamics. It's a law. The question is, as I've learned from my legal training, whose truth, which interpretation? The Supreme Court always comes down 5-4 on everything, right? True, because there are two interpretations. Basically, that's what-
cues.zh: 如果我不相信热力学第一定律，你们会把我赶出去。我会是终极的异端和狂热分子，我会被否定。我当然相信热力学第一定律。这是一条定律。问题是，正如我从法律训练中学到的，谁的事实，哪种解释？最高法院在所有事情上总是以5比4裁决，对吧？没错，因为有两种解释。基本上，那就是——

cues.en: The Supreme Court's fore is interpreting the law. The law is the law, but the interpretation is something else. So here are the two interpretations. If you eat it, you better burn it, or you're going to store it. If that's true, then this is a matter of energy balance. Energy balance, that's what everyone will tell you. And it's the result of two aberrant behaviors. Calories in gluttony, calories out sloth.
cues.zh: 最高法院的职责是解释法律。法律就是法律，但解释是另一回事。所以有两种解释。如果你吃进去了，最好把它烧掉，否则你就会把它储存起来。如果这是真的，那么这就是能量平衡的问题。能量平衡，每个人都会这么告诉你。而它是两种异常行为的结果。热量摄入是暴食，热量消耗是懒惰。

cues.en: That's what everybody assumes is if you're obese, well, you must eat too much or exercise too little or both, and therefore, it's your fault. That's what we believe. To this day, we still don't have insurance for obesity, although just today, you know that the AMA finally said obesity is a disease.
cues.zh: 大家都这么认为：如果你胖，那肯定是因为你吃得太多、动得太少，或者两者兼有，所以全是你的错。我们一直深信不疑。直到今天，针对肥胖仍然没有保险覆盖，虽然就在今天，AMA 终于承认肥胖是一种疾病了。

cues.en: This is funny because actually in 2004 HHS said obesity was a disease. It took the AMA nine years to catch up with HHS. Figure that out. It's based on this dogma. The dogma is that if you eat more than you burn, you'll gain weight. If you eat less than you burn, you'll lose weight because all calories are the same. A calorie is a calorie. This is the biggest pile of, you know what, there is. This is absolutely not true.
cues.zh: 这挺讽刺的，因为其实早在 2004 年 HHS 就已经认定肥胖是疾病了。AMA 整整花了九年才跟上 HHS 的步伐。大家想想看。这完全是基于一个教条。这个教条就是：摄入大于消耗就会长胖，摄入小于消耗就会变瘦，因为所有卡路里都一样。卡路里就是卡路里。这简直是一派胡言，绝对不是真的。

cues.en: But if you believe it, then the corollaries of a calorie is a calorie R, that this is free will. You get to choose what you put in your mouth. It's personal responsibility because if you're obese, you chose to be gluttony and sloth, that's your problem and diet and exercise will fix it. That's what everyone believes from a calorie is a calorie. And who says that a calorie is a calorie? Well, the food industry says a calorie is a calorie and that's because it serves them well.

That's the question. That's what we're going to try to answer now. In order to answer that, you actually have to know some science. I'm going to make this very brief and very quick. We're going to talk about these two hormones right over here called leptin and insulin. Leptin is a hormone that comes from your fat cell, goes to your brain and tells your brain you have enough energy on board to engage in normal,
cues.zh: 这些是生化层面的问题，最终表现为行为障碍。这并没有什么不同。贪食和懒惰背后的生化机理到底是什么？这就是核心问题。也是我们现在要试着解答的。要回答这个问题，你其实得懂一点科学常识。我会讲得非常简短、快速。我们要聊聊这边的这两种激素：瘦素和胰岛素。瘦素是由脂肪细胞分泌的激素，进入大脑并告诉大脑：你体内存有足够能量来维持正常的、

cues.zh: 高耗能代谢过程。你可以以正常速率消耗能量，而且感觉良好。它会告诉大脑你体内有充足的能量。如果你的瘦素下降，或者大脑感知不到瘦素，大脑就会认为这是在挨饿。都听懂了吗？胰岛素也同样有意思，因为胰岛素只对脂肪细胞传达一件事。它说：储存能量。而它对大脑说的则是另一番话。它对大脑说：停下来。

cues.en: I'm in the middle of metabolizing a meal. I don't need any more. Let me deal with what I got." And so it's part of the satiety signal. cues.zh: “我正在代谢上一餐呢，不需要更多了，先让我把现有的处理完。”所以它是饱腹感信号的一部分。它告诉脂肪细胞变大，同时告诉大脑别再喂脂肪细胞了。所以它具有双重作用，而正是这种双重作用，成了理解肥胖生理机制的关键。接下来我们就要讲讲这个。它的工作原理是这样的：我们得先解释一个悖论。悖论是这样的。在座谁有孩子？挺多人都举手了。

It's so important that if you don't eat it, your body makes it. That's how important it is. This guy over here is completely vestigial. There's not one biochemical reaction in the body that requires it, but it's very sweet and we like it a lot. The question is,
cues.zh: 一个果糖分子，一个六元环，一个五元环。这种物质对生命必不可少。地球上的每一个细胞都利用葡萄糖来获取能量。它重要到就算你不摄入，你的身体也会自行合成。它就是这么重要。而边上这个东西完全是多余退化的。人体内没有任何一个生化反应需要它，但它非常甜，我们又非常喜欢。问题是，

cues.en: What do we do with it if we don't need it for any biochemical reaction? That's one of the key questions. But over here is sucrose. This is table sugar, cane sugar, beet sugar, the stuff you put in your coffee. One glucose, one fructose. O-glycosidic linkage linking the two. The enzyme in your intestine, sucrose, cleaves this in about a nanosecond. So when you absorb the two moieties, they're exactly the same. And that's what all the data say, is that they're exactly the same. High fructose corn syrup and sucrose are metabolically equal.
cues.zh: 如果任何生化反应都不需要它，我们拿它怎么办？这是关键问题之一。但这边是蔗糖。这是食糖、甘蔗糖、甜菜糖，就是你放进咖啡里的那种。一个葡萄糖，一个果糖。O-糖苷键把两者连接起来。你肠道里的酶——蔗糖酶——大约一纳秒就把它切开。所以当你吸收这两个部分时，它们完全一样。所有数据都表明，它们完全一样。高果糖玉米糖浆和蔗糖在代谢上是等同的。

cues.en: metabolically bad, metabolically equally bad. This is what our consumption of fructose, so double it for sugar, has done over the last 100 years. Our ancestors getting-
cues.zh: 代谢上糟糕，代谢上同样糟糕。过去100年，我们的果糖摄入——如果是蔗糖就按双倍算——造成的结果就是这个。我们的祖先获取——

cues.en: Fruits and vegetables out of the ground with the occasional honey got about 15 grams of fructose per day. Prior to World War II with the nascent candy and soft drink industries in the country, we got up to about 20 grams per day. By 1977, we got up to 37 grams per day. This is just before high fructose corn syrup invaded our shores at 8% of total caloric intake. By 1994, we're up to 55 grams a day. That was 10% of total caloric intake, and adolescents currently consume 75 grams per day. That's 12% of caloric intake. And 25% of adolescents consume 100 grams.
cues.zh: 从地里获取水果蔬菜，偶尔吃点蜂蜜，每天大约摄入15克果糖。二战前，国内糖果和软饮料产业刚起步，我们每天摄入量升到约20克。到1977年，升到每天37克。这正好是在高果糖玉米糖浆涌入我国、占总热量摄入8%之前。到1994年，我们每天达到55克。那是总热量摄入的10%。而青少年目前每天摄入75克，占总热量摄入的12%。还有25%的青少年每天摄入100克。

cues.en: of fructose per day. Double that for sugar. That's 200 grams of sugar. Multiply by 4.1 calories per gram. That's 840 calories in sugar. cues.zh: 果糖，每天。如果是蔗糖，就翻倍。那就是200克糖。乘以每克4.1卡路里。就是840卡路里来自糖。所以按每天2000卡路里配额算，糖占了40%的热量。问题是，你能承受吗？你的肝脏能承受吗？你能在坏事发生前代谢掉所有这些糖吗？记住帕拉塞尔苏斯告诉我们的：剂量决定毒性。这会不会是用量过量？会不会危害你的健康？

cues.zh: 确实。所以在我看来，我们整个食品供应都被掺假了，和果糖有关，因为为了适口性而添加果糖，尤其是在降低脂肪时；而且显然还把它当作褐变剂，因为食物上色更好，对吧？你把它涂在烧烤肋排上，让它更好上色，对吧？还有焦糖化，你知道，我们喜欢那个。还有为了保质期和冷冻而去除纤维。我们还用反式脂肪做了替代，但那些正在减少，因为我们知道它们有毒，尽管它们仍然

cues.zh: 是合法的，而且仍在FDA的公认安全清单上。想想这是怎么回事吧，因为我们知道它们有毒。那么，糖会导致肥胖吗？会，也不会。食品行业会告诉你，什么都会导致肥胖；你知道吗，他们说得对。这是真的。因为看看Harvard School of Public Health的Mozaffarian这项研究，研究哪些食物导致体重增加最多：薯片和炸薯条。确实，我同意这一点。

And when a meta-analysis was done earlier this year from the University of Otago, you'll notice the diamond doesn't cross the identity line. That means that it's significant. So there is a significant increase in weight, but when you actually look at them, do the math, it's only 0.8 BMI points. Remember I told you.

cues.zh: 我们要处理七八个BMI点数。糖会导致体重增加吗？会。糖会导致肥胖吗？是一个因素。糖是肥胖的成因吗？差得远。问题在于，关键不是肥胖。记住，关键是代谢综合征，钱都花在那儿。我甚至不关心肥胖。

cues.en: What I care about is people getting sick because I'm a doctor. Here's the problem. Common wisdom says that sugar is just empty calories and you can get your discretionary calories from anywhere. The problem is that hepatic fructose metabolism is completely different from that of glucose. This is what the first YouTube video went into in exhausting detail and I will not repeat it. But I'm going to show you very quickly that chronic fructose exposure alone promotes the metabolic syndrome. This again is from that first video.
cues.zh: 我关心的是人们生病，因为我是医生。问题在这儿。常识说糖只是空热量，你可以从任何地方获取自由支配的热量。问题在于，肝脏的果糖代谢与葡萄糖完全不同。第一个YouTube视频详尽地讲了这一点，我不会重复。但我会很快展示，仅长期接触果糖就会促进代谢综合征。这同样来自第一个视频。

cues.en: When you consume glucose, say rice, white bread, starch, 80% of the glucose goes to all the organs of the body. Only 20% hits the liver. And where does it go? It goes to this guy over here, glycogen. Glycogen is liver starch. And liver starch, for lack of a better word, is good because that's your energy store for a rainy day. That's the first energy that's used when you fast. That's why marathoners carb load before a marathon race.
cues.zh: 当你摄入葡萄糖，比如米饭、白面包、淀粉，80%的葡萄糖进入全身器官，只有20%到达肝脏。然后它去哪？它去了这边这个家伙——糖原。糖原是肝淀粉。肝淀粉，没有更好的说法，是好的，因为那是你备用的能量储备。禁食时最先使用的能量就是它。这就是马拉松选手在赛前进行碳水负荷的原因。

cues.en: is to try to build up their glycogen stores because glycogen is non-toxic. So if you can up your glycogen stores, your liver has more energy in reserve. And that's a good thing.
cues.zh: 是为了尽量增加糖原储备，因为糖原无毒。所以如果你能提高糖原储备，肝脏就有更多储备能量。这是好事。

cues.en: Now, a little of it will sneak down here and get metabolized by the mitochondria and throw off a little of this stuff called citrate, and that will then get turned into liver fat. This process here in orange is called de novo lipogenesis, new fat making. This is how your liver turns carbohydrate into fat, is through this process here. But you're not dealing with very much carbohydrate here because it all went to glycogen, and most of it actually got metabolized elsewhere anyway. So your liver's protected. Everybody see that?
cues.zh: 现在，有一小部分会溜到这里，被线粒体代谢，释放出一点叫柠檬酸的东西，然后转化成肝脏脂肪。这里橙色的过程叫从头脂肪生成，也就是制造新脂肪。你的肝脏就是通过这里这个过程把碳水化合物变成脂肪。但这里处理的碳水并不多，因为大部分都去了糖原，而且其实大部分已经在别处被代谢掉了。所以你的肝脏受到保护。大家都看到了吗？

cues.en: Your liver is protected. So this is for lack of a better word is normal. Now let's talk about something that's not normal. This guy, alcohol. That's not normal. Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen. But alcohol is a toxin, right? It's two toxins in one. You wrap your Lamborghini around a tree, right? Acute alcohol toxicity. And you fry your liver. Chronic alcohol toxicity. We keep it out of the hands of children. Here's acute alcohol exposure. Here's acute sugar exposure. None.
cues.zh: 你的肝脏受到保护。所以这，姑且这么说，算是正常的。现在说点不正常的。这位，酒精。这不正常。碳、氢、氧。但酒精是毒素，对吧？它是两种毒素合为一体。你把兰博基尼撞到树上，对吧？急性酒精中毒。你把肝烧坏。慢性酒精中毒。我们不让儿童碰到它。这是急性酒精暴露。这是急性糖暴露。没有。

cues.en: Why? Because the brain doesn't use fructose for energy. It does use alcohol. But it doesn't use fructose for energy, so you don't get any of those CNS symptoms because it doesn't get there. So let's consume the same number of calories of alcohol. Now, most of them go to the liver instead of going to the periphery. And what happens to it? You see glycogen anywhere? No glycogen. It bypasses...
cues.zh: 为什么？因为大脑不用果糖供能。它确实会用酒精。但它不用果糖供能，所以你不会出现那些中枢神经系统症状，因为果糖根本到不了那里。那我们摄入同样卡路里的酒精。现在，大部分会去肝脏，而不是去外周。那它会怎样？你看到糖原了吗？没有糖原。它绕过……

cues.en: glycogen and goes down to the mitochondria and since there's so much of it, you get big time fat making and some of it won't make it out. cues.zh: 糖原进入线粒体，因为量太大，就会大量合成脂肪，有些还运不出去。于是就形成了脂滴，这就是酒精性脂肪性肝炎，你会合成大量甘油三酯，导致高甘油三酯血症，还会进入肌肉，造成肌肉胰岛素抵抗，同时也成为增重的底物。我们还知道，酒精对大脑有去抑制作用，让你喝得更多。“我就喝一杯”，最后却喝了五杯。

cues.zh: 它们都有一个特征。它们都是褐色的。很好。谢谢。它们全都是褐色的。这就是褐变反应，也就是美拉德反应。有人知道糖化血红蛋白（HbA1c）是什么吗？那是给糖尿病患者做的一项化验，用来监测血糖控制水平。本质上就是葡萄糖与血液中的蛋白质结合。没错，眼前这些也是一样的。这就是美拉德反应。葡萄糖与食物本身的蛋白质发生了结合。

cues.en: The common link is this browning or myard reaction or a non-enzymatic glycation. Here's the deal. You can think of it this way. cues.zh: 它们的共同纽带就是这种褐变反应，或者叫美拉德反应，也就是非酶糖基化。简单来说，你可以这样理解：你可以在 375 度下把肉烤上一小时，也可以在 98.6 度下把肉“烤”上 75 年。结果是一样的。我们都会变“焦黄”，这是衰老的一部分，是正常的生理老化，每个人都逃不过。

And if you had orange juice this morning, you're browning faster. That's the deal. And we know it. And we know it's true. Because every time this reaction occurs, you release a hydrogen peroxide. And that hydrogen peroxide does damage inside the cell, unless it's quenched by an antioxidant.
cues.zh: 问题在于，你变焦的速度有多快？如果你不信，来看个例子。这是新生儿的肋软骨，白白净净的。而这是 88 岁老人的肋软骨，已经完全变褐色了。如果你今天早上喝了橙汁，你褐变的速度就会加快。事实就是如此。我们清楚这一点，而且确信无疑。因为这种反应每发生一次，就会释放出一个过氧化氢分子。如果不被抗氧化剂清除，过氧化氢就会在细胞内造成损伤。

cues.en: But if you're deficient, which happens when you have a bad diet, then only sugar causes the problem. Starch doesn't. And you can see here in a non-alcoholic fatty liver disease clinic at Duke University, this is Dr. Manal Abdel-Malek's work showing that the grade of steatosis or fatty liver is dependent on how much fructose consumption, whether it's daily or not. cues.zh: 但如果你体内缺乏某些营养，比如饮食不良时就会这样，那么只有糖才会引发问题，淀粉不会。大家看这里，这是杜克大学非酒精性脂肪肝门诊的 Dr. Manal Abdel-Malek 的研究成果，显示脂肪变性（即脂肪肝）的严重程度取决于果糖摄入量，不论是否每天摄入都是如此。纤维化的阶段也是同理。好的。

cues.en: What's going on over there in Nevada? I guess you can only burn so much energy going like this. Here are the 10 most unhappy states in the nation. Here's the adult diabetes rate, here's the adult heart disease rate, and finally, here's soda per capita consumption. Now, what do you see? Pretty significant overlap, wouldn't you say? Yeah? Well, now, this is correlation, not causation, and I'm very clear on the difference. We're going to talk about the difference.
cues.zh: 内华达州那边是怎么回事？我猜光做这个动作也消耗不了多少热量。这里是全美最不幸福的 10 个州。这是成年人糖尿病发病率，这是成年人心脏病发病率，最后是人均汽水消耗量。现在，大家看到了什么？重合度相当高，不是吗？对吧？不过，这只是相关性，并不是因果关系，我很清楚两者的区别。我们接下来就来谈谈这个区别。

cues.en: The question is, which direction does it go? Is it that soda causes heart disease and diabetes, or is it that people with heart disease and diabetes like to drink soda? You can't tell. Because it's one snapshot in time, you can't tell which way the data went. True. Here's what's happening worldwide. This is global consumption of sugar and sugar crops. Here we are at 629 calories availability here in blue.
cues.zh: 问题是，因果方向到底朝哪边？是汽水导致心脏病和糖尿病，还是心脏病和糖尿病患者喜欢喝汽水？你无法判断。因为这只是某个时间点的快照，你无法判断数据的方向。没错。以下是全球正在发生的情况。这是全球糖和糖料作物的消费量。这里蓝色显示的是629卡路里的供应量。

cues.en: And here's the rest of the world. Now, the American Heart Association says 150 to 200 calories in added sugar per day. Right here, this color blue. How many countries are above that? How about all of them? In fact, that's why diabetes is going skyrocketing everywhere. So here's world sugar consumption tripling over the past 50 years. Per capita consumption, notice Brazil. Brazil used to be a poor country. They were always a sugar exporter.
cues.zh: 接下来是世界其他地区。美国心脏协会说，每天添加糖应摄入150到200卡路里。就在这里，这个蓝色。有多少国家高于这个水平？所有国家都超了？事实上，这就是糖尿病在各地飙升的原因。所以，过去50年全球糖消费量增长了两倍。人均消费量，注意巴西。巴西过去是个贫穷国家。他们一直是糖出口国。

cues.en: but they couldn't afford their own sugar. But now they can because they're a brick country. They sell Embraer jets and biodiesel and World Cup and all that stuff. The fact is that Brazil now has the highest increase in rate of prevalence of type 2 diabetes in the world. It doesn't have the highest prevalence. That's reserved for Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, and Malaysia. Why them? Why do they have the highest diabetes rates in the world?
cues.zh: 但他们买不起自己的糖。但现在他们可以了，因为他们是金砖国家。他们卖Embraer喷气机、生物柴油、世界杯之类的东西。事实是，巴西现在2型糖尿病患病率的增幅全球最高。它的患病率并不是最高。最高的是沙特阿拉伯、科威特、阿联酋、卡塔尔和马来西亚。为什么是它们？为什么它们有全球最高的糖尿病患病率？

cues.en: No alcohol, no alcohol. But they got soft drinks like they're going out of style. Why? Because it's hot and the water supply is a question mark and no alcohol. This is their reward. Now, the difference is alcohol, for lack of a better word, is self-limiting because you end up under the table. But soft drinks, you can drink them all day, right? And they do.
cues.zh: 不喝酒，不喝酒。但他们买软饮料，简直像不要钱一样。为什么？因为天气很热，而供水情况又是个问号，而且不能喝酒。这就是他们的奖励。区别在于，酒精，恕我找不到更好的说法，是会自我限制的，因为你最后会醉倒在桌子底下。但软饮料可以整天喝，对吧？而他们确实这么喝。

cues.en: and that's why they have diabetes. Now, how do I know that the sugar caused the diabetes? Because correlation is not causation, but we have causation too. This is our work, just came out three months ago, very proud of it. Sanjay Vasu, one of my colleagues at Stanford Prevention Institute and I, took four databases and melded them together. We took the Food and Agriculture Organization or FAO statistics database.
cues.zh: 所以他们才会得糖尿病。那我怎么知道是糖导致了糖尿病？因为相关性不等于因果关系，但我们也有因果证据。这是我们的研究成果，三个月前刚发表，我们对此非常自豪。我和同事 Sanjay Vasu 都在 Stanford Prevention Institute 工作，我们把四个数据库整合到了一起。我们采用了联合国粮食及农业组织，也就是 FAO 的统计数据库。

cues.en: from the World Health Organization, which for the whole decade, 2000 to 2010, which has food supply as total calories, fruits excluding wine, oils, roots, tubers, pulses, nuts and vegetables, meat, cereals, and sugar, sugar crops and sweeteners as separate items. We then linked that to the International Diabetes Federation statistics database for diabetes prevalence worldwide for the decade. And then we linked that to the World Bank Gross National Income Database to control for GDP,
cues.zh: 该数据库来自世界卫生组织，涵盖整个十年，也就是 2000 到 2010 年，记录了食物供应情况，包括总热量、水果（不含葡萄酒）、油类、根茎类、块茎类、豆类、坚果和蔬菜、肉类、谷物，以及单独列出的糖、糖料作物和甜味剂。接着，我们将其与 International Diabetes Federation 的统计数据库关联起来，获取这十年间全球糖尿病患病率的数据。然后，我们又将其与 World Bank 的国民总收入数据库关联起来，以控制 GDP、

cues.en: urbanization and aging, and then we linked that to a physical activity database to control for physical inactivity. We asked the question, what about the world's diet? Predicts diabetes prevalence change over time worldwide. That was our question. Everybody with me? Here's what we did. 204 countries, we had complete data for 154. The 50 that we did not use were no different from the 154 by a very fancy set of statistics.
cues.zh: 城市化和人口老龄化因素，之后还关联了一个身体活动数据库，以控制缺乏身体活动的影响。我们要研究的问题是：全球饮食结构的哪些因素，能够预测全球糖尿病患病率随时间的变化？这就是我们的问题。大家都跟上了吗？下面是我们的做法。我们分析了 204 个国家，其中 154 个国家的数据是完整的。根据一套非常复杂的统计方法，未纳入的 50 个国家与这 154 个国家并没有差异。

cues.en: We did a lot of statistics. This is called an econometric analysis. Now, standard percent versus percent would be called an ecological analysis. This is not an ecological analysis. This is an econometric analysis. This actually won two economists' Nobel Prizes for being able to predict stock market crashes based on what's happening before to predict what happens after, because there's causational inference in this.
cues.zh: 我们做了大量的统计分析。这被称为计量经济学分析。通常那种单纯百分比对百分比的比较，叫生态学分析。但我们做的不是生态学分析，而是计量经济学分析。这种方法其实帮两位经济学家拿了诺贝尔奖，它能根据先前发生的事情来预测后续的走势，从而预测股市崩盘，因为这其中包含因果推断。

cues.en: generalized estimating equations with a conservative fixed effects approach called the Hausmann test, a hazard model to control for selection bias called the Heckmann test. This is the important one. Since we had the whole decade, we didn't have a snapshot. We had the movie. And you can learn a whole lot more from a movie than you can from a snapshot, can't you? That's called the Granger Causality Test because we can determine what came first. Because you can't infer causation if something didn't come first.
cues.zh: 我们使用了广义估计方程，结合保守的固定效应方法（豪斯曼检验），以及用来控制选择偏差的风险模型（赫克曼检验）。但最关键的是下面这个：因为我们拥有整整十年的完整数据，所以我们看到的不是一张静态快照，而是一部完整的电影。相比单张快照，你显然能从电影里获取多得多的信息，对吧？这被称为“格兰杰因果检验”，因为我们可以由此确定先后顺序。毕竟，如果一件事不是发生在另一件事之前，你根本不可能推断出因果关系。

cues.en: Proximate cause, you need proximate cause. Period effects to control for secular trends. We did all this really, really neat statistical analysis and Sanjay Bessu is an absolute genius. What we did was we controlled for GDP, obesity, urbanization, aging, and physical activity. The question was, is it the obesity or is it something specific in the food supply? That was the question. During the decade,
cues.zh: 必须要有近因。我们还引入了时期效应来控制长期趋势。我们做了所有这些非常漂亮的统计分析，Sanjay Bessu 简直是个天才。具体来说，我们控制了 GDP、肥胖率、城市化水平、老龄化和体力活动等变量。当时的核心问题是：导致这一结果的到底是肥胖本身，还是食品供应中的某种特定成分？这就是我们要找的答案。在这十年间，

cues.en: Diabetes prevalence rose from 5.5 to 7 percent worldwide. Not good. Here's the effects model. Sugar plus controls plus period. Bottom line, remember that diamond that can't cross the identity line? Well, it doesn't. It's very significant. In fact, for every 100 calories, you increased your diabetes prevalence worldwide by 0.8 percent.
cues.zh: 全球糖尿病患病率从 5.5% 飙升到了 7%。这可很不妙。这是效应模型：糖分加上控制变量，再加上时期效应。结论是，还记得那个不能跨过基准线的菱形标记吗？它确实没有跨过去。结果极其显著。事实上，每人每天只要多摄入 100 大卡糖分，全球糖尿病患病率就会直接上升 0.8%。

cues.en: And here's the adjusted association when you took all the factors into account between sugar availability and diabetes prevalence. Here's what you need to take home. This is the take home slide. Only changes in sugar availability predicted those changes in diabetes prevalence worldwide. Only. If you consumed 150 calories extra per day in total calories, diabetes prevalence only went up by 0.1%. Nothing.
cues.zh: 这是考虑了所有因素之后，糖供应量与糖尿病患病率之间调整后的关联。你们需要记住的是：这就是结论页。全世界糖尿病患病率的变化，只有糖供应量的变化能够预测。只有这一点。如果你每天额外摄入总热量中的150卡路里，糖尿病患病率只会上升0.1%。几乎没有影响。

cues.en: But if those 150 calories happen to be a can of soda, diabetes prevalence went up 11-fold, 1.1%, and we're not consuming one can of soda per day, we're consuming two and a half. So that's 2.4%. Given that American diabetes rates are 8.3%, that means that 26% of all diabetes in America today is due to sugar and sugar alone.
cues.zh: 但如果这150卡路里恰好来自一罐汽水，糖尿病患病率就会上升11倍，也就是1.1%；而我们每天可不只是喝一罐汽水，我们喝的是两罐半。所以就是2.4%。鉴于美国的糖尿病率是8.3%，这意味着如今美国所有糖尿病病例中，有26%是由糖，而且只有糖导致的。

cues.en: not due to obesity, not due to total calories, sugar and sugar alone. You want to do something, you want something actionable, you want something that's going to change how much money we spend so we can salvage Medicare? Here it is. And of course, our government is doing absolutely nothing. Our data show that 25% of diabetes worldwide is explained by sugar. And more importantly, this is causation.
cues.zh: 不是肥胖，不是总热量，而是糖，只有糖。你想做点什么，想要一个可执行的方案，想要真正改变我们花费的金额，从而挽救 Medicare？方案就在这里。当然，我们的政府什么都没做。我们的数据显示，全世界25%的糖尿病可以用糖来解释。更重要的是，这是一种因果关系。

cues.en: because these data meet what's known as the Bradford Hill, the Austin-Bradford Hill criteria for what we call causal medical inference. Now, what does that mean? It means that you can show dose effect, you can show duration effect of sugar on diabetes, and you can show, most importantly, directionality. That is, those countries where sugar went up,
cues.zh: 因为这些数据符合所谓的 Bradford Hill，也就是 Austin-Bradford Hill 标准，这是我们所说的因果医学推断标准。那么，这意味着什么？这意味着你可以证明糖对糖尿病存在剂量效应，可以证明糖对糖尿病存在持续时间效应，而最重要的是，你可以证明方向性。也就是说，那些糖供应量上升的国家，

cues.en: showed an increase in diabetes rates. Those countries, the few of them where sugar went down, showed decreased diabetes rates and precedence, three-year time differential. So every country when their sugar went up, three years later you saw the change in diabetes in either direction. That's causal medical inference. Now, it's not scientific proof. So there are different kinds of proof.
cues.zh: 糖尿病率也随之上升。少数几个糖供应量下降的国家，糖尿病率也随之下降；而且还存在先后关系，时间差为三年。所以每个国家的糖供应量上升后，三年之后，你都会看到糖尿病发生变化，可能上升，也可能下降。这就是因果医学推断。不过，这还不是科学证明。因为证明有不同的类型。

cues.en: anecdotal data which of course is absolute garbage and you can't do anything with that because an N of one means nothing. Then there's correlation, but correlation suffers from this directionality question which came first because it's a snapshot and you can't tell. Then there's this thing called causal medical inference. We're going to talk about that right now. Then there's this thing called scientific proof that everybody keeps harping on. So in medicine today, what percentage of what we know
cues.zh: 轶事数据当然完全是垃圾，你拿它做不了什么，因为 N 为 1 毫无意义。然后是相关性，但相关性受制于方向性问题：谁先谁后？因为它只是一个快照，你判断不了。然后是所谓的因果医学推断。我们现在就来讲这个。然后是大家一直念叨的科学证明。那么在今天医学中，我们所知的有百分之多少

cues.en: is scientifically based, evidence-based, scientific proof, randomized controlled trials. That's the standard. How much of what we know, what percent of what we know today is due to scientific proof? What do you think? Want to give me a percentage? 10. 10. Good. 10. 10% of what we know is due to randomized controlled trials. That means 90% of what we know is causal medical inference. So here's a question. What level of proof do you need?
cues.zh: 是有科学依据、基于证据、科学证明、随机对照试验的？这才是标准。我们所知的有多少，今天我们所知的有多大比例来自科学证明？你们觉得呢？想给我个百分比吗？10。10。好。10。我们所知的 10% 来自随机对照试验。这意味着我们所知的 90% 是因果医学推断。所以问题来了。你需要什么级别的证明？

cues.en: You tell me. Who here believes in global warming? Why? Got any proof? Causal inference. Can you randomize control trial and show me that that's what's going on? No. Who here believes that football trauma causes Alzheimer's? How come? You got proof? Causal inference. Who here believes that tobacco causes lung cancer? How come? You got proof?
cues.zh: 你告诉我。这里谁相信全球变暖？为什么？有证据吗？因果推断。你能做随机对照试验，向我证明事情就是这样吗？不能。这里谁相信橄榄球创伤会导致阿尔茨海默病？为什么？你有证据吗？因果推断。这里谁相信烟草会导致肺癌？为什么？你有证据吗？

cues.en: Who's done the randomized control trial where you take naive people and expose them to cigarette smoke for the next 50 years and see what their lung cancer rates are? Number one, it would be too expensive. Number two, it would be damn unethical, wouldn't it? In fact, most of these studies would be damn unethical. You ever think we're going to get the actual scientific studies, the scientific proof for sugar-causing diabetes? Number one, nobody's got a zero baseline. Nobody's naive. Number two, this is something that happens over 40, 50, 60 years.
cues.zh: 谁做过这样的随机对照试验：找一群未接触过的人，让他们暴露在香烟烟雾中 50 年，然后看他们的肺癌发生率？第一，太贵了。第二，那会非常不道德，对吧？事实上，这类研究大多都会非常不道德。你有没有想过，我们真能拿到糖导致糖尿病的实际科学研究、科学证明吗？第一，没有人是零基线。没有人是未接触过的。第二，这是在 40、50、60 年里发生的事。

cues.en: How are you going to keep people on the same diet for that long, and how are you going to figure out what they actually ate when we can't even figure it out after one day? Don't you think that would be a little unethical to do that to people? You'll never get these data. But of course, the food industry says, well, we don't have the data, we need more research. We always need more research. Of course, we need more research. The question is, do we have enough proof to act?
cues.zh: 你怎么可能让人们长期坚持同一种饮食？连他们一天吃了什么我们都弄不清，又怎么搞清楚他们长期到底吃了什么？这样对待受试者，难道不觉得有点违背伦理吗？你根本拿不到这种数据。但食品工业当然会说：哎呀，我们还没有数据，需要更多研究。我们永远都需要更多研究。当然需要更多研究。问题是，我们现有的证据足够支撑我们采取行动了吗？

cues.en: Them saying we need more proof is them moving the goalposts because we'll never get enough proof for them. The question is, what do you think? Do you think we have enough? We have causal medical inference for sugar and diabetes. Do we have enough? It's for you to decide. Okay, addictive. The last piece of this. Binging on high calorie foods may be as addictive as cocaine or nicotine and could cause compulsive eating and obesity according to a study.
cues.zh: 他们说需要更多证据，其实是在不断拔高门槛，因为对他们来说证据永远都不够。问题在于，你怎么看？你觉得现在的证据够了吗？关于糖和糖尿病，我们已经有了医学上的因果推断。证据够不够？这由你来决定。好，成瘾性。这是最后一部分。一项研究表明，暴饮暴食高热量食物的成瘾性可能堪比可卡因或尼古丁，并可能导致强迫性进食和肥胖。

cues.en: Here are all these books that came out on obesity and addiction and reward. They're all popular books based on no data. But what do you think? You think that science could catch up to this? Here's neuroimaging studies, PET scanning of dopamine receptors. Dopamine is the feel-good neurotransmitter, the pleasure neurotransmitter in the reward center here. Here's a control brain with nice hot-
cues.zh: 看看市面上这些关于肥胖、成瘾和奖赏机制的书。它们全是没有任何数据支持的畅销书。但你怎么看？你觉得科学能证实这些观点吗？来看看这些神经影像学研究，多巴胺受体的 PET 扫描。多巴胺是让人感觉良好的神经递质，是大脑奖赏中心传递愉悦感的递质。这是一个对照组的大脑，有着非常活跃的——

cues.en: dopamine receptors, which is good. Here's a cocaine brain where they've been damped down. This is the neuroanatomic equivalent of the phenomenon of tolerance because dopamine down regulates its own receptor. Once this happens, you need more substrate to get the same effect. That's called tolerance. Then, of course, when you withdraw it, now you can get withdrawal and you get symptoms. Everybody with me? Well, here's a control brain and here's an obese brain. What do you see? Same thing.
cues.zh: 多巴胺受体，这很好。而这是一个吸食可卡因者的大脑，受体已经被抑制了。这就是“耐受”现象在神经解剖学上的体现，因为多巴胺会下调自身的受体。一旦发生这种情况，你就需要更多物质才能获得相同的效果。这就叫耐受性。当然，一旦停用，就会产生戒断反应并出现症状。大家听明白了吗？好，这是一个对照组大脑，这是一个肥胖者的大脑。你看到了什么？一模一样。

cues.en: Not quite as bad, but same concept. So this is the reward system. Here's the ventral tegmental area here where the dopamine neurons live, and here's the nucleus accumbens where the dopamine information gets received. So how fast this gets transduced has everything to do with what level of reward you achieve with any given stimulus, whether it be power or gambling or shopping or cocaine or alcohol or, for that matter, sugar.
cues.zh: 虽然没那么严重，但原理是一样的。这就是奖赏系统。这里是腹侧被盖区，也就是多巴胺神经元聚集的地方，而这里是接收多巴胺信号的伏隔核。这个转导过程有多快，直接决定了你在某种刺激下能获得多大程度的奖赏感，不管这种刺激是权力、赌博、购物、可卡因、酒精，还是糖。

cues.en: This just shows what happens. Here's that dopamine neuron, and you see it's going blip, blip, blip, right? You add nicotine, blip, blip, blip, blip, you get more reward. That's basically what we're talking about. That's why people start smoking. Then, of course, the dopamine receptors go down, then they can't stop smoking. That's addiction. Food intake is a readout of reward because here's injecting morphine.
cues.zh: 这张图展示了具体发生的过程。这是多巴胺神经元，你可以看到它在“嘟、嘟、嘟”地放电，对吧？加入尼古丁后，它就“嘟嘟嘟嘟”加速放电，你获得了更多奖赏。基本就是这么个原理。人们就是这样开始吸烟的。当然，随之而来的是多巴胺受体减少，接着他们就戒不掉了。这就是成瘾。食物摄入其实反映了奖赏程度，因为如果把吗啡注射……

cues.en: into the reward center and you can see that as the morphine goes up, the food intake goes up because food intake is a readout of reward. You can see that all the reward centers are all linked together into the nucleus accumbens including the hypothalamus, which is the starvation area, the amygdala, which is the fear area, and of course the reward area. So hunger, reward, and stress, all reasons to eat.
cues.zh: 到奖赏中枢，你会看到随着吗啡增加，进食量也跟着上升，因为食物摄入就是奖赏程度的体现。可以看到，所有的奖赏中枢最终都连接到了伏隔核，包括主管饥饿的下丘脑、主管恐惧的杏仁核，当然还有奖赏区本身。所以饥饿、奖赏和压力，全都是促使我们进食的原因。

cues.en: and they all conspire against us all at the same time. When we see a patient in our clinic, that's the question we ask ourselves. Is this patient obese because they're hungry? I know what to do about that. Or is this patient obese because of the reward system is defective and they're addicted? That's a lot harder to deal with, but we know how to do that too. Or is this person eating because of stress?
cues.zh: 而且它们总是在同一时间联手对付我们。我们在门诊接诊患者时，总会先问自己这个问题：这位患者肥胖是因为饥饿吗？对此我知道该怎么处理。还是因为奖赏系统出了故障，导致他们成瘾了？这要棘手得多，但我们也知道怎么应对。又或者这位患者吃东西纯粹是因为压力？

cues.en: which is enormous problem, especially in America. And that one's a really hard one. Because it's not the stress, it's the response to stress. So if you think you're stressed, you're stressed, whether you are or you're not. And most kids today are stressed like never before. And you know what stresses them the most? Facebook. And this is going on in every animal. Here's humans right there, big dopamine receptors here. When obese, dopamine receptors go down.
cues.zh: 这是个巨大的问题，尤其在美国。而这个问题真的很难。因为关键不是压力，而是对压力的反应。所以如果你觉得自己有压力，你就有压力，不管实际有没有。现在大多数孩子承受的压力前所未有。你知道什么最让他们有压力吗？Facebook。这在每种动物身上都会发生。这里是人类，多巴胺受体很丰富。肥胖时，多巴胺受体会下调。

cues.en: Here are bonnet macaques, same thing, and here are rats, same thing. Bottom line, obesity means downregulation of dopamine receptors, which means you need more food to get the same level of reward, or you might as well crawl in a hole and die. That's what it's all about. These people are eating because their brain says they have to. The question is, is fast food addictive? What do you think? Yes. No? What do you think? We actually looked at that question.
cues.zh: 这里是帽猴，也一样；这里是老鼠，也一样。结论是，肥胖意味着多巴胺受体下调，这意味着你需要更多食物才能获得同样的奖赏水平，否则还不如钻进洞里等死。事情就是这样。这些人吃东西，是因为他们的大脑说必须吃。问题是，快餐会成瘾吗？你们觉得呢？会。不会？你们觉得呢？我们确实研究过这个问题。

cues.en: Everybody would familiar with this book? Michael Moss put this out. Salt, sugar, fat, how the food giants hooked us. This is wrong. This is a mistake because there's one thing not on the list. What's missing? Caffeine. Now, we've got fast food. Salt, sugar, fat, and caffeine. The question is, of these four, which are addictive? Let's talk about salt. Is salt addictive? No, it's not addictive. In humans,
cues.zh: 大家都熟悉这本书吗？Michael Moss 出的。《盐、糖、脂肪：食品巨头如何让我们上瘾》。这不对。这是个错误，因为清单上少了一样东西。少了什么？咖啡因。现在我们有快餐：盐、糖、脂肪和咖啡因。问题是，这四样里哪些会成瘾？先说盐。盐会成瘾吗？不会，它不成瘾。在人类身上，

cues.en: The threshold is physiologically fixed. Higher levels are attributable to preference, but you can alter that preference. Lots of people do, especially when they have to go low salt for some reason. And we know because we take care of a disease in endocrinology called salt-losing congenital adrenal hyperplasia, where their kidneys are losing salt non-stop. But when we give them the salt-retaining hormone that works in the kidney called aldosterone, their salt intake goes way down. And if they were addicted, that wouldn't happen. So when we fix their physiology,
cues.zh: 阈值在生理上是固定的。更高的摄入水平可归因于偏好，但这种偏好可以改变。很多人都会改变，尤其是因为某些原因必须低盐饮食时。我们知道这一点，因为我们在内分泌科治疗一种叫失盐型先天性肾上腺增生症的疾病，患者的肾脏会不停失盐。但当我们给他们一种在肾脏起作用的保盐激素——醛固酮时，他们的盐摄入量会大幅下降。如果他们成瘾了，这就不会发生。所以当我们纠正他们的生理状态时，

cues.en: Their preference gets a lot better. Salt, not addictive. Now let's take fat. Is fat addictive? What do you think? Nope. Rodents binge but show no signs of dependence. In humans, they always binge on high fat, high carb, or high sugar items like pizza and ice cream. You don't binge on high fat per se. Otherwise, the Atkins diet would have everybody addicted and they'll tell you, they're losing weight. How could they lose weight if they were all addicted?
cues.zh: 他们的偏好会大大改善。盐，不成瘾。现在看看脂肪。脂肪会成瘾吗？你们觉得呢？不会。啮齿动物会暴食，但没有依赖迹象。在人类身上，他们总是暴食高脂肪、高碳水或高糖的食物，比如披萨和冰淇淋。你不会单纯对高脂肪暴食。否则，阿特金斯饮食法会让所有人都上瘾，而他们会告诉你，他们在减肥。如果他们都上瘾了，怎么可能减肥？

cues.en: Energy and density actually has a stronger association with obesity and metabolic syndrome than fat does. So, fat? Not addictive. So we're left with these two. Caffeine? Oh man, caffeine's addictive. And if you take my Starbucks away from me, I will kill you.
cues.zh: 能量密度其实比脂肪与肥胖和代谢综合征的关联更强。所以，脂肪？不上瘾。那就只剩这两样了。咖啡因？天呐，咖啡因会上瘾。谁要是抢走我的 Starbucks，我跟他没完。

cues.en: Model drug of dependence, gateway drug in fact. Dependence shown in children, adolescents, adults, 30 percent who consume it meet the DSM criteria for dependence and physiologic addiction is well established with the headache and the test performance and everything else. Mega addictive. But do you see anybody going out and regulating Starbucks or Pete's or anything like that? Why? Because it's not toxic. It's addictive but not.
cues.zh: 堪称依赖性药物的典型，事实上更是一种“入门药物”。儿童、青少年、成年人都表现出了依赖性，30% 的饮用者符合 DSM 的依赖诊断标准，伴随头痛、测试表现下滑等症状的生理成瘾也早已被证实。超级上瘾。但你见过有人站出来监管 Starbucks 或者 Pete's 这一类的吗？为什么？因为它没毒。它会上瘾，但没——

cues.en: toxic unless you mix it with alcohol and then you got something called four loco and that we're banning. Everybody got it? When it's toxic and addictive, we ban it or we regulate it. Caffeine alcohol together, that's a bad deal. But caffeine alone, keep your hands off my Starbucks. Caffeine, yes, addictive. That leaves this one, sugar. Is sugar addictive? What do you think? We've known this for a long time because anybody know what this is?
cues.zh: 毒，除非你把它跟酒精混在一起，搞出一种叫 Four Loko 的东西，那个我们是要封禁的。大家明白了吧？当一样东西既有毒又让人上瘾时，我们就会禁掉或监管它。咖啡因加酒精，那可是个糟糕的组合。但单独喝咖啡因，别打我 Starbucks 的主意就行。咖啡因，确实上瘾。那就只剩下这一个了，糖。糖会上瘾吗？你们觉得呢？我们其实早就知道答案了，有谁知道这是什么吗？

cues.en: It's called sweeties. Sweeties. This is a super concentrated sucrose sugar solution that you dip the pacifier in and you put in the newborn baby boy's mouth before you do the circumcision because it releases opioids and it deadens the pain. This has been known forever. Then you mix it with a little wine and then you got a real good cocktail.
cues.zh: 这叫 Sweeties。Sweeties。这是一种超高浓度的蔗糖溶液，在给刚出生的男婴做割礼前，把安抚奶嘴往里蘸一下，再塞进婴儿嘴里，因为它能促使释放阿片类物质并止痛。这早就人尽皆知了。要是再兑上一点酒，那可就是一杯相当地道的鸡尾酒了。

cues.en: Is there really such a thing as sugar addiction? Well, we have to look for similarities to other drugs of dependence like nicotine, morphine, amphetamine, cocaine. The one I think is most appropriate is alcohol because after all, alcohol and sugar are basically metabolized the same way because after all, where do you get alcohol from? Fermentation of sugar, it's called wine. We do it every day up in Napa Sonoma. The big difference between alcohol and sugar is that for alcohol, the yeast does the first step of metabolism called glycolysis.
cues.zh: 糖瘾这回事真的存在吗？我们得找它和其他成瘾药物的相似之处，比如尼古丁、吗啡、安非他命、可卡因。我觉得最合适的是酒精，因为酒精和糖基本上走同样的代谢路径，毕竟酒精从哪来？糖发酵，就叫葡萄酒。我们在纳帕和索诺玛每天都这么干。酒精和糖最大的区别是，酒精的第一步代谢——糖酵解——由酵母完成。

cues.en: For sugar, we do our own first step. But after that, when the mitochondria see it, it doesn't matter where it came from. And that's the point. And that's why they both cause the same diseases. And they do the same thing to the brain. So for the criteria for addiction in animals are binging, withdrawal, craving, and then this one down here called cross-sensitization with other drugs of abuse. That means that if you expose an animal to one drug of abuse, like cocaine, for three weeks, and a dictum,
cues.zh: 对糖来说，第一步由我们自己完成。但之后线粒体看到它时，不管它从哪来。关键就在这。所以它们会导致同样的疾病，对大脑做同样的事。动物成瘾的标准是暴食、戒断、渴求，还有下面这个：与其他滥用药物交叉敏化。意思是，如果你让动物接触一种滥用药物，比如可卡因，持续三周，并让它成瘾，

cues.en: Then you expose them to a second drug they've never seen before like, say, amphetamine. They're addicted to the amphetamine even though they've never seen it before because the dopamine receptors are already down regularly because they're the same dopamine receptors. Everybody got it? Does sugar do this? Absolutely. QEDs slam dunk sugar is addictive in animals. What about humans? Who saw this movie? Do you like it? More or less? I have a big problem with this movie.
cues.zh: 然后让它接触第二种从没见过的药，比如安非他命。它会对安非他命上瘾，尽管从没见过，因为多巴胺受体已经下调了，因为它们就是同一批多巴胺受体。都明白了吗？糖会这样吗？绝对会。QED，板上钉钉，糖在动物中会成瘾。那人类呢？谁看过这部电影？喜欢吗？多多少少？我对这部电影有很大意见。

cues.en: Because if you watch the movie, his doctor, Morgan's doctor, keeps saying, you got to get off this high-fat diet, high-fat diet, high-fat diet, high-fat diet, high-fat diet. Not the high-fat diet. It's the high-sugar diet. High-sugar diet. That's what caused all the problems. So, can sugar be addictive? Watch. I was feeling bad in the car. Feeling like... Sorry. Really. I was feeling really, really sick and unhappy.
cues.zh: 因为如果你看过那部电影，他的医生，Morgan 的医生，一直说，你得戒掉这种高脂饮食，高脂饮食，高脂饮食，高脂饮食，高脂饮食。不是高脂饮食。是高糖饮食。高糖饮食。那才是所有问题的根源。那么，糖会让人上瘾吗？看。我在车里感觉很难受。感觉像……抱歉。真的。我当时真的、真的又难受又不开心。

cues.en: Started eating, feel great. Feel really good now. I feel so good, it's crazy. Isn't that right, baby? Yeah, you're afraid, don't I? This was on day 18, okay, of his 30-day sojourn through McDonald's. He just described withdrawal. That's withdrawal. And he needed another hit in order to feel good again. He just described withdrawal. He was a vegan, right, because his girlfriend was a vegan chef. And in 18 days, he's a sugar addict. So, you tell me.
cues.zh: 一开始吃，感觉棒极了。现在感觉真的很好。我感觉太好了，简直离谱。对吧，宝贝？是啊，你怕了，不是吗？这是他 30 天麦当劳之旅的第 18 天，好吧。他刚才描述的就是戒断反应。那就是戒断反应。他需要再来一口才能重新感觉良好。他刚才描述的就是戒断反应。他本来是纯素食者，对吧，因为他女朋友是纯素食厨师。结果 18 天后，他就成了糖瘾者。你说呢。

cues.en: So this is what we're dealing with. We are dealing with an industry that wants us to consume its product. Well, gee, every industry wants us to consume their product in some fashion or another. The question is, what if it hurts you? What if it hurts you?
cues.zh: 所以这就是我们要面对的东西。我们面对的是一个想让我们消费其产品的行业。哎，每个行业都想以某种方式让我们消费他们的产品。问题是，如果它伤害了你呢？如果它伤害了你呢？

cues.en: So here, this is an example. This is the Federal Trade Commission versus Sugar Information back in 1972. This was an arm of the Sugar Research Association. The fat time of day, you're really hungry and ready to eat two of everything. Here's how sugar can help. Any data? They can advertise any way they want. They're allowed. How about this one? The birth of the Uncola. Why we have the youngest customers in the business? Seven up. You okay with that?
cues.zh: 所以这里有个例子。这是 1972 年的 Federal Trade Commission 诉 Sugar Information 案。它是 Sugar Research Association 的一个分支。一天中容易发胖的时刻，你真的很饿，准备把什么都吃两份。糖可以这样帮上忙。有数据吗？他们想怎么打广告就怎么打。这是被允许的。这个怎么样？Uncola 的诞生。为什么我们拥有这个行业里最年轻的顾客？Seven up。你能接受吗？

cues.en: But this was going on. How about this one? This was in Publix, supermarket chain in Florida just a year ago. Drinks are on us. Publix is rewarding top grades with free apple juice and soda students. We salute your thirst for knowledge. Well, the American Heart Association gets it, and I am a proud member of the American Heart Association because they get it. The fat hypothesis has been debunked, and they have taken it back.
cues.zh: 但这种情况一直在发生。这个呢？这是一年前佛罗里达州连锁超市Publix里的情况。饮料我们请客。Publix用免费苹果汁和汽水奖励成绩优异的学生。我们向你们的求知欲致敬。美国心脏协会懂了，而我是美国心脏协会的自豪成员，因为他们懂了。脂肪假说已被推翻，他们也收回了。

cues.en: 2010, American Journal of Clinical Nutrition, Krause et al. But this is dietary sugar intake and cardiovascular health. I was a co-author of this and very proud to have been so. We recommend a reduction in sugar consumption from 22 teaspoons of added sugar per day down to either nine for males or six for females. That's a reduction by two-thirds to three-quarters. How are we going to do that? How are we going to ever accomplish that? Especially since
cues.zh: 2010年，《美国临床营养学杂志》，Krause等人。但这是关于膳食糖摄入与心血管健康。我是这项研究的合著者，非常自豪。我们建议将糖消费量从每天22茶匙添加糖降至男性9茶匙或女性6茶匙。也就是减少三分之二到四分之三。我们怎么做得到？我们到底怎样才能实现？尤其是因为

cues.en: We don't even know we're consuming it because only one-third of our total added sugar intake comes from sugar-sweetened beverages like soda, juice, sports drinks. One-sixth comes from things that we call desserts, you know, candy, ice cream, things like that. That means one-half of our sugar consumption is hidden in foods that we didn't even know had sugar like salad dressing. Yogurt is a big one. Anybody here think yogurt is healthy? I got a bridge to sell you. Plain yogurt.
cues.zh: 我们甚至不知道自己摄入了糖，因为总添加糖摄入中只有三分之一来自含糖饮料，比如汽水、果汁、运动饮料。六分之一来自我们称为甜点的东西，比如糖果、冰淇淋之类的。这意味着我们一半的糖消费隐藏在我们甚至不知道含糖的食物中，比如沙拉酱。酸奶是大头。这里有人觉得酸奶健康吗？我有座桥要卖给你。原味酸奶。

cues.en: Sure. You want to take some whole fruit and mix it in with plain yogurt like they do in Europe? No problem. Off you go. Okay? But processed yogurt, you know, the stuff they're selling on the shelves in the supermarket? Take a look. Just take a look at the amount of sugar. Now, it's total sugar, so some of it's lactose, which is milk sugar. The question is, how much of it is lactose and how much of it is added sugar? You can't know. You're not allowed to know.
cues.zh: 当然可以。你想拿点新鲜水果拌进原味酸奶里，像欧洲人那样吃？完全没问题，尽管吃。对吧？但加工酸奶呢，也就是超市货架上卖的那些？去看一眼吧。就看一眼那含糖量。现在上面标的是总糖量，所以其中一部分是乳糖，也就是奶类天然带的糖。问题在于，这里面有多少是乳糖，又有多少是添加糖？你根本不可能知道。你根本不被允许知道。

cues.en: Because the food industry won't let you know. Because in 1989, the food industry lobbied the Food and Drug Administration when they were coming out with the Nutrition Labeling and Education Act of 1990. And they said, if we told our consumers, our customers, how much added sugar we put in each of our processed foods, our competitors could duplicate our recipes. This is proprietary information and you're not allowed to know it. And you know what the FDA said?
cues.zh: 因为食品行业不让你知道。因为在 1989 年，食品行业游说了美国食品药品监督管理局（FDA），当时 FDA 正准备出台《1990年营养标签与教育法案》。食品企业说：如果我们告诉消费者、告诉客户，我们在每种加工食品里加了多少糖，竞争对手就会复制我们的配方。这是专有商业机密，你没权利知道。你知道 FDA 怎么说的吗？

cues.en: Sure. This just shows. Here's what you need to know. Of the 600,000 items in the American grocery store today, 80% of them are spiked with added sugar. And that's not for our purposes, that's for the industries. Because they know when they add it, you buy more. For all the reasons that we've just discussed. And, worse yet, there are 56 names for sugar. And you don't know them. And you're not allowed to know them.
cues.zh: 行，随你。这正好说明了问题。你需要知道的是：如今美国杂货店里的 60 万种商品中，有 80% 都偷偷加了添加糖。这可不是为了我们着想，全是为了食品工业的利益。因为他们知道，只要加了糖，你就会买得更多。就因为我们刚才讨论的那些原因。更糟糕的是，糖有整整 56 种不同的叫法。而你根本认不出来。你也不被允许认出来。

cues.en: Does anybody know what Florida crystals are? Sugar. Anybody know what evaporated cane juice is? If you evaporate cane juice, what do you get? You get sugar. That's what they use in yogurt because cane juice must be healthy. Juice for cane. Here's how your food dollars have been bastardized and reallocated for you. Meats. This is 1982, 30 years ago. Here's 2012.
cues.zh: 有人知道 Florida crystals 是什么吗？糖。有人知道 evaporated cane juice 是什么吗？把甘蔗汁蒸发掉，会得到什么？糖。酸奶里用的就是这个，因为甘蔗汁肯定很健康。甘蔗的汁。看看你的食品支出是怎么被篡改、重新分配的。肉类。这是 1982 年，30 年前。这是 2012 年。

cues.en: Meats down 10% because of the low-fat directive. Fruits and vegetables, the same. Everybody says eat your fruits and vegetables. You know what? We're eating just as much as we were before. Grains and baked goods, 13 to 14%. Everybody says it's all the carbohydrate. What's only up a little bit? Dairy products, 13 down to 10% because now everyone's lactose intolerant. Processed foods and sweets, 11.6, 22.9, a doubling in 30 years.
cues.zh: 肉类下降了 10%，因为低脂饮食的指导方针。水果和蔬菜也是一样。人人都说要多吃水果和蔬菜。你知道吗？我们吃的量和以前一样多。谷物和烘焙食品，从 13% 增加到 14%。人人都说，问题都在碳水化合物。哪一项只略有增加？乳制品，从 13% 降到 10%，因为现在人人都有乳糖不耐受。加工食品和甜食，从 11.6% 增加到 22.9%，30 年翻了一倍。

cues.en: what's happened. That's the change, and that's what we're talking about tonight. Because processed food is high sugar, low fiber, and real food is low sugar, high fiber. And every diet that works is low sugar, high fiber, because every diet that works is real food. That's what this is about. This is a processed food disaster. But the food industry is making money off it. In fact, lots of it.
cues.zh: 事情就是这样。这就是变化，也是我们今晚要讨论的内容。因为加工食品含糖量高、纤维少，而真正的食物含糖量低、纤维多。所有有效的饮食法都低糖、高纤维，因为所有有效的饮食法吃的都是真正的食物。重点就在这里。这是一场加工食品灾难。但食品行业正从中赚钱。事实上，赚得非常多。

cues.en: Because here's the S&P 500 over the last five years. Here's the economic downturn of 2008 right here. And here's the stock price of McDonald's, Coke, and Pepsi. They're doing very well, thank you. And here's General Mills, Hormel, ConAgra, Kraft, Procter & Gamble, Archid Daniels, Midland. I said Hormel, I think, already. Bottom line, they're all doing better than the S&P. Want to make money? Invest in a food company. Because they have a winning formula for getting you to eat more.
cues.zh: 因为这是过去五年里的标普 500 指数。这边是 2008 年的经济衰退。这是 McDonald's、Coke 和 Pepsi 的股价。它们经营得非常好，谢谢。还有 General Mills、Hormel、ConAgra、Kraft、Procter & Gamble、Archid Daniels、Midland。我刚才好像已经提过 Hormel 了。总之，它们的表现都比标普指数好。想赚钱吗？投资食品公司。因为它们有一套让你吃得更多的制胜公式。

cues.en: Back to that first law. Remember, it's not about common sense. It's about the science. So let's restate it. Let's reframe the argument. If you're going to store it, that is, an obligate weight gain due to energy deposition, the most obvious of which is high insulin, and you know where that came from, and you expect to burn it, that is, normal energy expenditure for normal quality of life, because energy expenditure and quality of life are synonymous. Things that make your energy expenditure go up make you feel good, like...
cues.zh: 回到热力学第一定律。记住，这无关常识，而是关乎科学。所以我们换个说法，重新审视一下这个论点。如果你要把能量储存起来——也就是因能量沉积而必然导致的体重增加，最典型的就是高胰岛素，大家都知道它是怎么来的——同时你还打算去消耗能量，也就是维持正常生活质量所需的正常能量消耗，因为能量消耗和生活质量是划等号的。能让你提高能量消耗的事情会让你感觉良好，比如……

cues.en: ephedrine off the market, caffeine for two hours, exercise. Things that make your energy expenditure go down make you feel lousy. Hypothyroidism, starvation. If you're going to store it, energy deposition, and you expect to burn it, then you're going to have to eat it. Same first law, but now reinterpreted based on the science, not the common sense. Because the aberrant behaviors are a result of our biochemistry.
cues.zh: 已退市的麻黄碱、能管两小时的咖啡因、运动。而那些降低能量消耗的事物则会让你感觉糟糕透顶，比如甲减、挨饿。如果你要把能量储存起来（能量沉积），同时又打算去消耗它，那你就必须把它吃进去。同样是第一定律，但现在是基于科学而非凭常识重新诠释的。因为异常行为是我们体内生物化学机制作用的结果。

cues.en: and our biochemistry is a result of our changed environment. The only way we're going to fix it is to change the environment back. Here's a list of diseases. Every one of these was a personal responsibility disease until the sheer weight magnitude and gravity and the money that went into it made it very clear that it was a public health crisis instead. Here are some more newer ones.
cues.zh: 而我们的生化机制，又是环境改变的结果。解决这个问题的唯一途径，就是把环境扭转回来。这里有一份疾病清单。清单上的每一种病都曾被归咎于个人责任，直到其惊人的规模、严重性以及投入的巨额资金清楚地表明，这实际上是一场公共卫生危机。这里还有一些更新的病症。

cues.en: And these are very clearly personal responsibility diseases, right? Except they're not. They're public health crises. How about this one down here? What do you think about guns? It's San Francisco, so I know what you think about guns. But John Howard, the Australian prime minister, perhaps the most conservative politician in the last hundred years in any country, banned assault weapons in Australia back in the late 90s.
cues.zh: 这些显然是个体责任的疾病，对吧？但其实并非如此。它们是公共卫生危机。下面这个例子呢？你如何看待枪支问题？这里是旧金山，所以我知道你们对枪支的看法。但澳大利亚前总理约翰·霍华德，或许是过去一百年来任何国家中最保守的政治家，在90年代末在澳大利亚禁止了攻击性武器。

cues.en: And he was on CNN about two months ago, and they asked him, I mean, how could you do that? You're a conservative, you know, politician, libertarian. How could you ban guns? And he said, look, this is not a Democratic issue. This is not a Republican issue. This is not a liberal issue. This is not a conservative issue. This is a public safety issue. That's exactly right. Even he got it. Even he got it. But we don't get it. Well, this is a public safety issue because we will have no Medicare.
cues.zh: 大约两个月前，他接受了CNN的采访，他们问他，我的意思是，你怎么能这样做？你是个保守派，你知道，政治家，自由主义者。你怎么能禁枪呢？他说，看，这不是民主党的问题。这不是共和党的问题。这不是自由派的问题。这不是保守派的问题。这是公共安全的问题。完全正确。连他都明白了。连他都明白了。但我们不明白。嗯，这是公共安全问题，因为我们将会没有医疗保险。

cues.en: So the questions I'm going to leave you with, I have two homework assignments for you. Can our toxic food environment be changed without government or societal intervention, especially when there are potentially addictive substances involved? Has education worked for any substance of abuse? Not one. Did Nancy Reagan's just say no work? Does the Surgeon General's warning on a pack of cigarettes stop people from smoking? No. The thing that stopped people from smoking was secondhand smoke.
cues.zh: 所以，我要留给你们的思考题，我有两个家庭作业。我们的有毒食品环境能在没有政府或社会干预的情况下改变吗，特别是当涉及潜在成瘾物质时？教育对任何滥用物质有效过吗？一个也没有。南希·里根的“just say no”运动有效吗？卫生局局长的香烟包装警告能阻止人们吸烟吗？不能。阻止人们吸烟的是二手烟。

cues.en: When it started, when your smoking affected me, that's when we started getting legislation. And then the tobacco documents came out and we realized there was corporate malfeasance involved. That's when things changed. But not one lick of education made any difference in the amount of tobacco consumed. And Stan Glantz right here at UCSF showed that very nicely. Second question, can we afford to wait? The food industry will say, we need more research.
cues.zh: 当它开始影响到你，当你的吸烟影响到我时，我们才开始制定相关法律。后来烟草行业的文件曝光了，我们意识到其中存在企业不当行为。事情就是从那时开始改变的。但没有任何一点教育让烟草消费量发生变化。UCSF 的 Stan Glantz 就在这里很好地证明了这一点。第二个问题是：我们等得起吗？食品行业会说，我们需要更多研究。

cues.en: We need more research. Of course they're going to say we need more research. It's moving the goal post. Can we afford to wait to enact these public health measures when health care will be bankrupt due to chronic metabolic disease in just 13 short years? That's your homework assignment. This is my second to last slide. This is a paper that just came out in Lancet in March.
cues.zh: 我们需要更多研究。他们当然会这么说。这样做是在不断改变目标。医疗保健系统将在短短 13 年内因慢性代谢疾病而破产，在这种情况下，我们等得起再采取这些公共卫生措施吗？这就是你们的课后作业。这是我的倒数第二张幻灯片。这是一篇今年 3 月刚发表在《Lancet》上的论文。

cues.en: Profits and pandemics, prevention of harmful effects of tobacco, alcohol, and ultra-processed food and drink industries. What it says is that what we used to practice was called the old medicine and we focused on infections as the problem and microbes as the vectors. Now, the new medicine is all about chronic disease and the vector has changed. It is now multinational corporations instead. That's who we're battling.
cues.zh: 《利润与大流行：预防烟草、酒精以及超加工食品和饮料行业造成的危害》。它讲的是，我们过去采用的医疗模式被称为旧医学，重点关注感染这一问题，以及作为传播媒介的微生物。如今，新医学关注的全是慢性病，而传播媒介也变了。现在，它变成了跨国企业。这就是我们要对抗的对象。

cues.en: So for further reading, I refer you to a whole bunch of academic articles, and more academic articles, and more academic articles, and more academic articles, and more academic articles, and more academic articles. And finally, non-academic, if you choose to pick it up. Fat Chance, which was written for the public, but really, to be honest with you, I wrote it for doctors. My publisher says, you cannot write a book for doctors. We won't publish it. I said, okay, fine. I'll write it for the public.
cues.zh: 关于进一步阅读，我推荐了一大批学术文章，还有更多学术文章，更多学术文章，更多学术文章，更多学术文章，更多学术文章。最后还有非学术读物，如果你愿意拿起来读的话。Fat Chance 是面向大众写的，但老实说，我其实是写给医生的。我的出版商说，你不能写一本给医生看的书。我们不会出版它。我说，好吧，没问题。那我就写给大众。

cues.en: But I really wrote it for doctors because the whole medical profession has to change. And the problem is they bought the bill of goods that the food industry was selling and we got to fix it because a calorie is not a calorie. It never was and never will be. So lastly, we have started a nonprofit very specifically to provide medical, nutritional, and legal analysis and consultation to promote personal and public health against big food.
cues.zh: 但我其实是为医生写的，因为整个医学界都必须改变。问题在于，他们轻信了食品行业推销的那套说辞，而我们得纠正它，因为卡路里并不等于卡路里。过去不是，将来也不会是。所以最后，我们成立了一个非营利组织，专门提供医疗、营养和法律分析与咨询，促进个人和公共健康，对抗食品巨头。

cues.en: called the Institute for Responsible Nutrition. There's our website and contact me if you would like any more information. I want to thank my collaborators here at UCSF, the Weight Assessment for Teen and Child Health Clinic, where we do the actual boots on the ground changes in people's lives to actually make kids better. Stanford Prevention Institute, my colleague Sanjay Basu, who is an absolute genius.
